checks.claim: A Fresnel lens bends a lamp's light into a narrow beam that can be seen far out at sea.
checks.why: Rings of prisms bend the lamp's light into a parallel beam; the first one (Cordouan, 1823) was seen more than 20 miles out.

sources.title: Inside Science: The remarkable lens in America's oldest lighthouse station

checks.claim: Lighthouse lenses rotate so the beam sweeps around and flashes in a pattern.
checks.why: The lamp stays steady and the rotating Fresnel lens makes the flashes; flash panels and rotation speed set each light's characteristic.

sources.title: Ponce Inlet: Understanding how lighthouse lenses work

checks.claim: Large rotating lighthouse lenses were floated on a bath of liquid mercury to turn smoothly.
checks.why: From 1890 (Bourdelles) heavy optics floated on an annular mercury trough so they turned almost without friction and faster.

checks.claim: Foghorns warn ships with sound when fog hides a lighthouse's light.
checks.why: No light is visible in thick fog, so lighthouses added sound signals (cannon, bells, whistles, foghorns) to warn ships.

sources.title: Chesapeake Chapter US Lighthouse Society: Foghorn
